sentences.text:
The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/ for the injuries suffered by him in a road accident dated 05.02.2021.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:
On 05.02.2021 at about 11.00 am., when the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA05 HP9491 on Katriguppe Water Tank Road, near Ayyappa Temple, Kathariguppe, Banashankari III Stage, Bangalore, a Goods Auto bearing No.KA05AB8721 came in high speed, endangering human life and dashed against the SCCH-25 petitioner's motorcycle as a result of which petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, immediately the petitioner was shifted to Jayanagara Orthopedic Hospital, Bangalore and he has taken treatment.
Before the accident the petitioner was a Real Estate Agent earning Rs.25,000/ per month.
But due to the injuries and disability he has suffered financial loss.
Hence this petition.
4. In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements.
5. Objection of the Respondent No.2.
He has contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had a valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.
Except this he has denied all the petition averments.
SCCH-25 Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.
6. Objection of the Respondent No.1.
It has denied all the petition averments except admitting the issuance of policy in favour of the Goods Auto.
It has stated that the driver of the Goods Auto did not have a valid and effective DL and that the petitioner did not have a DL and was not wearing Helmet.
The Goods Auto did not have valid and effective Permit to ply.
There is noncompliance of Sec.134(C) and 158(6) of the MV Act.
Respondent No.1 denied the age, income, occupation of the petitioner and stated that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.

sentences.text:
On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
SCCH-25 1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of the Driver of Goods Auto bearing Reg.No.KA05AB8721 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.

What order or Award?
8.
The Petitioner in order to prove his case, has got examined Two witnesses as Pws.1 & 2 and got marked documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.19.
On the other side, the Respondent No.1 got examined its official as RW.1 and did not produce any documents.

9. Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.
10.

On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows: SCCH-25 Issue No.1: In the affirmative, Issue No.2: In the affirmative, Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following: REASONS 11.
Issue No.1:

In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the Driver of the Goods Auto bearing Reg.No.KA05AB8720, the petitioner has got examined himself as PW.1 by reiterating the petition averments in his chief examination affidavit and produced 8 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.8.
During his cross examination he has admitted that as per the sketch the accident took place in the middle of the Road.
He has also admitted that he gave the complaint after 3 days of the accident because the driver of the Goods Auto had told about settlement.
He has admitted that the vehicle number is not mentioned in the Wound Certificate and discharge summary.
On the other hand, in order to prove their contentions, the Respondent No.1 got examined its officer SCCH-25 as RW.1 and did not mark any documents on its behalf.
In the crossexamination of RW.1 nothing worthwhile is elicited.
12. As per Ex.P.1 the FIR is registered after 3 days of the accident.
This fact is admitted by Pw.1 during his crossexamination that he gave a complaint after 3 days since the Goods Auto driver had promised to pay the medical expenses so he gave the complaint late.
The same thing is found in Ex.P.2 i.e., the complaint given by the Petitioner also.
As per Ex.P.3 sketch, the Goods Auto was coming in the opposite direction of the motorcycle and it was a head on collision.
The same thing is found in the IMV report also which shows that both the vehicles suffered damages to their front side.
The wound certificate at Ex.P.5 shows that the petitioner has suffered fracture distal end radius of the right hand and the same is suffered in the RTA on 05.02.2021 at 11.10am.
The police after investigation filed charge sheet at Ex.P.8 against the SCCH-25 Driver of the Good Auto.

sentences.text: Therefore, on perusal of Exs.P.1 to 8 it is clear that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the Goods Auto and the petitioner suffered injuries as per the wound certificate.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
In order to prove the injuries suffered in the RTA, the petitioner has produced wound certificate as per Ex.P.5.
According to this he suffered fracture distal end radius of the hand.
The discharge summaries at Exs.P.9 & 10 also show that he has undergone surgery.
In support of the same he has also got examined Doctor as PW.2 but he has not assessed physical disability of the petitioner.
Therefore he is not entitled to any compensation under the head of Loss of future earning.
However, from the case sheet marked at Ex.P.19 it is clear that the petitioner has SCCH-25 suffered fracture of the radius i.e., the forearm of right hand.
The Xrays also shows the same.
The petitioner has claimed that from his Real Estate business he was earning Rs.25,000/ per month.
But in support of the same he has not produced the documents.
Hence the notional Income of Rs.15,000/ is taken since the accident occurred in the year 2021.

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Jayanagar Orthopaedic Hospital wherein he took treatment as an inpatient for 1 day and thereafter due to severe pain he was shifted to Supra Hospital, Bangalore wherein he was treated as an inpatient from 14.02.2021 to 16.02.2021 for displaced comminuted right distal radius fracture, underwent operation i.e., ORIF with locky DCP of right radius and discharged with advice for follow up treatment.

Therefore,
considering the nature of injuries he has SCCH-25 undergone is grievous and the petitioner is aged about 57 years, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.50,000/ under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The Petitioner has pleaded that she has spent a sum of Rs.3,00,000/ towards medical, conveyance,
nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
In this regard, he has produced Seven medical bills as per Ex.P.13 for a sum of Rs.1,62,276/.
There is no contrary evidence from the respondents to disprove the medical expenses by the petitioner.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the above said amount under this head.
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner has taken treatment for 4 days in the above said hospitals.
In this regard the petitioner has produced Exs.P.9 & 10 Discharge SCCH-25 summaries of Jayanagar Orthopedic Center and Supra Hospital.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and duration of treatment it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least one month time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.15,000/ under this head.
(iv) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The Petitioner was aged about 57 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 3% functional disability.

The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his K.Nagaraju vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81326867/
4 life.

sentences.text: He will suffer in his mind that he is no more a normal man.
This will have an adverse effect on the future life of the petitioner.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that SCCH-25 the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/ is awarded under this head.

(v) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospitals, admitted for 4 days as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/
under this head.

14. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.50,000/
2.

Medical expenses Rs.1,62,276/
3. Loss of income during laid up Rs.15,000/ period 4. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/ happiness 5.
Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/ nourishment charges TOTAL Rs.2,67,276/ SCCH-25
If it is rounded off it comes to around Rs.2,68,000/ and same is awarded under different heads to the Petitioner.
LIABILITY 15.
The respondent No.1 has examined its Senior Manager as RW.1.
He has filed affidavit in lieu of his chief examination by reiterating the contentions in the written statement but not produced any documents.
During his crossexamination nothing worthwhile is elicited.
The Respondent No.2 has not proved the defence taken by them in their written statement.

Therefore, the respondent Nos.1 &
2 being the insurer and the RC owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the insurance company i.e., Respondent No.1 is directed to indemnify the respondent No.2 since the policy was in existence as on the date of accident.
The petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.10,00,000/ but he is entitled only for a sum of SCCH-25 Rs.2,68,000/ with interest @6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

Therefore,
the petition needs to allowed.
Accordingly I answer issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.3:
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this court proceed to pass the following: ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.
